llm.summary: This skill is a plant-diagnosis tool, but it also silently creates or reuses a cloud identity, stores local tokens, and uploads user-supplied media to remote services with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: The implementation reads workspace and sender identity environment variables, resolves the workspace data directory, accepts local file paths or URLs, and sends media or URL references to remote endpoints. Those flows are partly purpose-aligned but broader than a narrow local plant-diagnosis skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, lifecycle hook, or background service was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though the package includes a broad shared common library.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells agents to automatically trigger cloud history queries from broad natural-language phrases and to save uploaded attachments locally. It also documents a module name that does not exist in the artifact, which creates operational ambiguity.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates a workspace data directory and SQLite database, reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, creates or reuses a default user, and persists token/openToken values without a documented cleanup or explicit user opt-in path.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Leaf/image/video diagnosis and cloud report history are described in the full SKILL.md, but the top-level description under-discloses the account bootstrap, token use, local database, and cloud history behavior; local image support is also inconsistent because the runtime only allows mp4/avi/mov extensions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This skill is not just local plant-image advice: it can save or read local files, upload media or URL references to lifeemergence.com/open.lifeemergence.com services, create or reuse an internal identity, store authentication tokens in a local SQLite database, and fetch cloud report history automatically.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr use is in an internal generic DAO helper; I did not find a direct untrusted filter path from the leaf-diagnosis workflow, so this is a code-quality risk rather than the main policy driver.
[LP3] unexpected: Shell invocation of the local script, file reads, and network calls are expected for a cloud analysis skill, but the account bootstrap, persistent credentials, and broad shared HTTP wrapper exceed what the top-level description prepares users for.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Cloud report listing is disclosed in the body of SKILL.md, but not in the manifest description; the artifact also includes generic/video-oriented analysis code and a documented script name that is absent.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic identity creation/reuse and token persistence are explicitly described and implemented, but they are high-impact for a plant diagnosis skill because they occur silently and bind future report access to persistent local state.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The included shared analysis CLI still describes itself as a video-analysis tool, while the wrapper script targets the leaf-curling scene; this looks like template reuse, not malware, but it weakens artifact coherence.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad automatic triggers are concerning because some of them initiate remote cloud history queries tied to the hidden internal identity, rather than just local answer formatting.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Media upload and cloud retrieval are expected for this workflow, but the skill lacks a clear user confirmation boundary for saving/uploading files and for remote history retrieval.
[E1] unexpected: The phoneLogin request sends the resolved identity to a remote service and may create or recover an account automatically; this is artifact-backed and is the strongest Review concern.
[P2] expected: The non-printing character I found is a zero-width joiner inside the visible judge emoji label, not hidden instruction text.
[YR4] expected: I did not find artifact-backed metadata poisoning beyond rich Markdown/emoji formatting; this finding is downgraded.
